The law behind the register Lei n.º 19/97 (Lei de Terras) art. 8 · Lei n.º 8/2026 (Lei do Petróleo) art. 75 · Lei n.º 12/2022 (Lei de Electricidade) art. 43 · Decreto n.º 36/2001 · Decreto n.º 31/2012 · IFC Performance Standard 5

Already in the law

The 50 m strip your register is measured against

Mozambican law draws a strip of land along every pipeline and power line. What is built inside it is a cost, a delay or a dispute waiting to happen, and the earlier you know, the cheaper it is to deal with.

Under the Land Law, the land occupied by oil, gas, water, electricity and telecommunications conduits, with a strip of 50 metres on each side, is a zona de protecção parcial (Lei n.º 19/97, de 1 de Outubro, art. 8(g)). Protection zones are public domain (art. 6), and no land-use right (DUAT) can be acquired in them, only special licences (art. 9).

The sector laws repeat the strip. The Petroleum Law makes the 50 m around petroleum infrastructure a partial protection zone and leaves the safety zone to regulation (Lei n.º 8/2026, art. 75(3)–(4)). The Electricity Law sets an administrative servitude of up to 50 m from the line’s axis, registered in the land cadastre and the property register (Lei n.º 12/2022, art. 43). On the Pande–Temane gas corridor, a 200 m safety zone applies on each side, and building there needs the project operator’s prior consent (Decreto n.º 36/2001, arts. 2–3).

The 50 m partial protection zone, explained

Why it matters

What builds up between visits

Settlement follows roads, and many pipelines and lines run beside them. New houses, machambas and stalls appear inside the strip between patrols, and each one becomes somebody’s cost.

A house in the zone today is a compensation line tomorrow

The Petroleum Law provides compensation for damage to crops, buildings and improvements in the zone (Lei n.º 8/2026, art. 75(5)) and puts resettlement costs on the rights holder (art. 61). Knowing where structures stand while they are few keeps those costs small.

The date decides what is owed

Under the Electricity Law, no compensation is due to people who acquired their rights after the line was built (Lei n.º 12/2022, art. 43(10)). A dated register of what stood in the servitude, and when, is the record that question turns on.

Your census teams need to know where to go

Resettlement starts with identifying the area and its current occupation (Decreto n.º 31/2012, art. 19). A register made from the air tells field teams where the structures are before they arrive, so the census and asset inventory are planned on facts.

The chair of EDM, the national electricity utility, has described the ocupação desenfreada das zonas de protecção parcial, the unchecked occupation of the protection zones along transmission lines, as a serious constraint that drives up compensation and resettlement costs (AIM, 29 September 2023).

What you receive

A register your land, servitude and GIS teams can use

  • Each structure listed with an ID, its distance to the line, its band, its chainage and its coordinates in WGS84 and in the route’s UTM zone (36S or 37S in Mozambique).
  • Every 500 m rated high, medium or low for encroachment density, so the servitude team knows where to go first.
  • The imagery named, and dated where the source gives a date.
  • A PDF report in Portuguese or English, with maps, the segment table, a photo of each structure and the coordinate register.
  • GIS layers in GeoPackage, GeoJSON, KMZ and Shapefile, and an interactive map file that opens in a browser, including in the field.

Our standard

Land and assets, never people

AfriScan maps what is on the land: structures, cleared ground, excavations and tracks. We do not identify, count or follow people, and whether a structure is authorised is for you and the authorities to decide. We write construções, never invasões.

A person reviews every result

Building datasets and detection models propose; a reviewer confirms, corrects and adds. What the imagery cannot settle is listed for a ground check.

Dated and credited

Every report names its imagery and, where the source provides it, the capture date. Map-service basemaps are never passed off as survey imagery.

Scheduled, never “real‑time”

Satellites and drones capture images on particular dates, so re-surveys follow a schedule agreed with you, with a notice of what changed.

Supports your processes

Our registers support regularisation, community engagement, legal processes and IFC Performance Standard 5 cut-off-date records. They are not cadastral surveys.

Satellite first, drones where the permits allow

Two routes to the picture, and the rules for each

Satellite and your own imagery. A survey starts from your route file and dated satellite imagery, open building datasets or the orthophotos you already hold. No one travels and no drone flies, however long the route. This is the practical route along long corridors and where access is restricted.

Drone detail. Where a stretch needs more detail than satellite imagery shows, Afridrone surveys it, subject to the permits and authorisations each job requires. In Mozambique those come in layers: IACM approval of the operation under its RPAS directive, authorisation of the survey itself by the Minister of National Defence (Lei n.º 6/2024, art. 13(1)(b)), and authorisation to release the data to you (art. 13(2)). The original data of such a survey are State property (art. 14(1)).

Afridrone is working towards the operator approvals Mozambique requires. Every drone proposal sets out the authorisations that particular survey needs and how long they take, so the schedule is honest from the start.

Drone law in Mozambique

For procurement and compliance teams

Local content, data and tenders

Oil and gas work in Mozambique runs under the local-content rules of the new Petroleum Law and Lei n.º 9/2026, which reach subcontractors as well as rights holders. Drone survey data also carry the deposit and release rules of Lei n.º 6/2024. Our procurement notes set out what applies to this kind of service and what to ask any supplier for.

Notes for procurement teams

We respond to tenders, RFQs and RFPs. Send your supplier or prequalification forms with your request; the proposal states which registrations are in place for your contract and which are being arranged. Reports and deliverables are available in Portuguese or English.

Frequently asked questions

Which widths do you measure in Mozambique?

By default we report structures within 50 m and 100 m of the line, which covers the partial protection zone of the Land Law and a band outside it where pressure builds. We add the 200 m safety zone on the Pande–Temane corridor (Decreto n.º 36/2001), the width recorded in your concession or servitude, or any company standard, up to six widths in one survey.

Does a satellite-only survey need authorisation under Lei n.º 6/2024?

Lei n.º 6/2024 regulates aerial surveys and defines them by reference to sensors on board manned or unmanned aircraft, so satellite-only work appears to fall outside it. CENACARTA also has a general role in approving geospatial production, so we treat this as a point for your counsel to confirm, and say so in the proposal. See drone law in Mozambique.

Can the report be in Portuguese?

Yes. The PDF report is available in Portuguese or English, so the same register can go to your land team, the district government and the Serviços de Cadastro. The GIS layers open in QGIS, ArcGIS and Google Earth.

Can you show which structures appeared after the line was built?

Where dated imagery exists from before and after the date that matters, yes. We compare dated scenes, flag new and removed structures automatically and have a reviewer confirm each one. This matters under the Electricity Law, which owes no compensation to people who acquired their rights after the line was built (Lei n.º 12/2022, art. 43(10)). Archive coverage varies by place and year, and we tell you what exists before you commit.

Do you work near LNG plants or in the north?

Satellite work needs no one on site, so a baseline can start where access is slow or restricted. Results go only to the contacts you name, and we never publish maps of your sites or of the settlements around them without your written permission. Drone flights near LNG plants, processing facilities or military sites need the operator’s permission and Defence authorisation, and some sites cannot be overflown at all.

Will you publish our route or imagery?

No. We never publish a client’s route, imagery or results without written permission. Lei n.º 6/2024 also makes reproducing aerial photographs, mosaics or orthophotos without authorisation an infraction (art. 16(1)(c)), which is why this site shows no Mozambican drone orthophotos.

Know what stands in your protection zone before it becomes a compensation claim.

Send the route or site boundary (KML, KMZ, GeoJSON, Shapefile, GPX or GeoPackage), the province and the widths that matter: 50 m, 100 m, 200 m or your concession's. We reply with a scope, an imagery plan and a written proposal.
